classification.difficultyReason: Model decreasing monthly sales as a geometric series and subtract the first ten terms from its limiting sum.

content.prompt:
A factory has been advertising its unbreakable widgets every month.

The first advertisement brought in 1000 sales, but every successive advertisement is only bringing in 90% of the previous month's sales.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How many widget sales will the advertisements 'eventually' bring in?

answer.worked:
$a=1000$, $r=0.9$. Since $|r|<1$, a limiting sum exists.

$$\begin{align*}S_\infty&=\frac{a}{1-r}\\S_\infty&=\frac{1000}{1-0.9}\\S_\infty&=10000\end{align*}$$

The advertisements will eventually bring in 10 000 sales.

children.label: b
children.prompt: About how many eventual sales were not brought in by the first 10 advertisements?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}S_{10}&=\frac{1000(1-0.9^{10})}{1-0.9}\\S_{10}&=6513.215599\\S_\infty-S_{10}&=10000-6513.215599\\S_\infty-S_{10}&=3486.784401\\S_\infty-S_{10}&\approx3487\end{align*}$$

About 3487 eventual sales were not brought in by the first 10 advertisements.
